epithet.en: Second daughter, sharp wit and fine eyes
epithet.da: Anden datter, skarp vid og smukke øjne

1.modern-en: Her father teases that Lizzy is his favorite. Mrs. Bennet disagrees, insisting she is no better than her sisters.

2.modern-en: Mentioned in family conversation about Mr. Bingley's visit. Her father jokingly puts in a good word for her.

3.modern-en: Overhears Darcy dismiss her as 'passable, but not attractive enough to tempt me.' Tells the story with great spirit among friends.

4.modern-en: Discusses the ball with Jane. Elizabeth is more perceptive about the Bingley sisters' true nature than Jane.

5.modern-en: Talks with Charlotte Lucas about Jane and Bingley. They differ on whether Jane should show her feelings more openly.

6.modern-en: Darcy begins to find her attractive, particularly her 'fine eyes.' She is unaware and continues to dislike him.

7.modern-en: Jane falls ill at Netherfield. Elizabeth walks three miles through muddy fields to nurse her, arriving with dirty petticoats.

8.modern-en: Stays at Netherfield to tend Jane. The Bingley sisters mock her behind her back, but Darcy defends her fine eyes.

9.modern-en: Mrs. Bennet visits and embarrasses the family. Elizabeth is mortified by her mother's behavior.

10.modern-en: Engages in witty exchanges with Darcy at Netherfield. She teases him about his pride; he grows more attracted.

11.modern-en: Walks about the room with Miss Bingley. Darcy admits Elizabeth could tempt him, unsettling both women.

12.modern-en: Returns home with Jane. Darcy is relieved, feeling she is becoming a danger to his peace of mind.

13.modern-en: Learns Mr. Collins is coming to visit. She is amused by his absurd letter.

14.modern-en: Endures Mr. Collins reading aloud from Fordyce's Sermons. Finds him ridiculous.

15.modern-en: Mr. Collins shifts his matrimonial attention toward her after learning Jane may be spoken for. Meets Wickham in Meryton.

16.modern-en: Has a long conversation with Wickham at the Philipses' party. He tells her Darcy cheated him of a living. She believes every word.

17.modern-en: Tells Jane about Wickham's story. Jane tries to see both sides; Elizabeth is firmly on Wickham's.

18.modern-en: Dances with Darcy at the Netherfield ball. Brings up Wickham; Darcy goes cold. The evening is a cascade of family embarrassments.

19.modern-en: Receives and firmly rejects Mr. Collins's proposal. He cannot believe any woman would refuse him.

20.modern-en: Her father supports her refusal; her mother is furious and threatens never to see her again.

21.modern-en: Receives a letter from Caroline Bingley announcing the whole party has left Netherfield for London, hinting at Darcy's sister for Bingley.

22.modern-en: Shocked that Charlotte Lucas has accepted Mr. Collins's proposal. Feels the friendship is damaged.

23.modern-en: Reflects on Charlotte's choice. Jane still has no word from Bingley. Mrs. Bennet's nerves are frayed.

24.modern-en: Jane writes from London saying she called on Miss Bingley, who was cold and distant. Elizabeth suspects the sisters are keeping Bingley away.

25.modern-en: Mrs. Gardiner warns Elizabeth about Wickham, who has no fortune. Elizabeth half-jokes that she will try to be sensible.

26.modern-en: Learns Wickham is now pursuing Miss King and her £10,000. Elizabeth defends him to Mrs. Gardiner but feels the sting.

27.modern-en: Travels to Hunsford to visit Charlotte. Stops in London and sees Jane's quiet sadness over Bingley.

28.modern-en: Arrives at Hunsford. Finds Charlotte's life with Collins surprisingly well-managed, if unenviable.

29.modern-en: Dines at Rosings and meets Lady Catherine de Bourgh. Stands her ground against Lady Catherine's imperious questioning.

30.modern-en: Darcy and Colonel Fitzwilliam arrive at Rosings. Elizabeth notices Darcy watching her and is puzzled.

31.modern-en: Gets along well with Colonel Fitzwilliam. Darcy keeps seeking her out at Rosings gatherings.

32.modern-en: Darcy visits the parsonage when she is alone. The conversation is awkward. Charlotte suspects he is in love with Elizabeth.

33.modern-en: Keeps running into Darcy on her walks. Colonel Fitzwilliam reveals that Darcy boasted of separating Bingley from an unsuitable match. Elizabeth is furious.

34.modern-en: Darcy proposes, insulting her family in the process. She rejects him angrily, accusing him of ruining Jane's happiness and Wickham's prospects.

35.modern-en: Receives Darcy's letter explaining his actions: Wickham is a liar who tried to elope with Georgiana, and he separated Bingley from Jane because he genuinely believed Jane indifferent.

36.modern-en: Rereads the letter and is forced to admit she has been blind and prejudiced. Realizes Wickham deceived her and Darcy may have been right about Jane appearing indifferent.

37.modern-en: Last days at Hunsford. She and Darcy part civilly but distantly.

38.modern-en: Leaves Hunsford with Maria Lucas. Meets Jane in London before heading home.

39.modern-en: Returns to Longbourn. Lydia prattles about officers; Elizabeth is weary of it.

40.modern-en: Confides in Jane about Darcy's proposal and letter, except the part about Bingley. Jane is astonished.

41.modern-en: Tries to warn her father against letting Lydia go to Brighton with the regiment. He dismisses her concerns.

42.modern-en: Joins the Gardiners on a tour of Derbyshire. Reluctantly agrees to visit Pemberley, believing Darcy is away.

43.modern-en: Tours Pemberley and hears the housekeeper praise Darcy warmly. Darcy arrives unexpectedly and is strikingly kind and attentive. She begins to see him differently.

44.modern-en: Darcy introduces her to Georgiana. Bingley's sisters are barely civil, but Darcy is all warmth. She realizes her feelings are changing.

45.modern-en: Visits Georgiana at Pemberley. Miss Bingley tries to upset her by mentioning Wickham; Georgiana goes pale. Elizabeth handles it with grace.

46.modern-en: Receives Jane's letters revealing Lydia has eloped with Wickham. She tells Darcy in distress, blaming herself for not exposing Wickham. He leaves abruptly.

47.modern-en: Rushes home with the Gardiners. Fears she has lost Darcy forever because of her family's disgrace.

48.modern-en: At home. The family is in crisis. Elizabeth reflects on how differently she now sees Darcy.

49.modern-en: Learns Lydia and Wickham are to be married. Suspects Mr. Gardiner paid Wickham off. Realizes this scandal may cost her Darcy permanently.

50.modern-en: Mr. Bennet returns home, chastened. Elizabeth hears the settlement terms and guesses far more money was involved than her uncle could afford.

51.modern-en: Lydia returns, shameless and boastful. She lets slip that Darcy was at her wedding, then claps her hand over her mouth.

52.modern-en: Writes to Mrs. Gardiner and learns the truth: Darcy found Wickham, paid his debts, bought his commission, and arranged the marriage — all for Elizabeth's sake.

53.modern-en: Bingley and Darcy return to Netherfield. Elizabeth is nervous and self-conscious around Darcy. Mrs. Bennet is insufferably rude to him.

54.modern-en: Darcy is quiet during the Bingleys' visit to Longbourn. Elizabeth cannot tell if he still cares. Mrs. Bennet snubs him openly.

55.modern-en: Bingley proposes to Jane. Elizabeth is thrilled for her sister. She and Darcy have not yet spoken privately.

56.modern-en: Lady Catherine arrives to demand Elizabeth promise never to accept Darcy. Elizabeth refuses to make any such promise, standing her ground completely.

57.modern-en: Hears from Mr. Collins that Lady Catherine is outraged. Mr. Bennet finds the idea of Darcy proposing hilarious. Elizabeth is quietly anxious.

58.modern-en: Walks with Darcy and they finally speak openly. She thanks him for saving Lydia. He proposes again and she accepts, telling him her feelings have completely changed.

59.modern-en: Confesses the engagement to Jane, who is overjoyed. That evening, tells Mr. Bennet, who is shocked and concerned she may not truly love Darcy.

60.modern-en: Explains to her father how her feelings changed. Mrs. Bennet is ecstatic. Elizabeth writes to Mrs. Gardiner with the happy news.

61.modern-en: Marries Darcy. They settle at Pemberley. Jane and Bingley move nearby. Georgiana becomes like a sister. Even Lady Catherine eventually comes around.

epithet.en: Master of Pemberley, proud and reserved
epithet.da: Herre til Pemberley, stolt og reserveret

3.modern-en: Arrives at the assembly ball. Initially admired for his wealth and looks, then despised for his pride. Dismisses Elizabeth as 'not attractive enough to tempt me.'

4.modern-en: Described as proud and reserved, in contrast to Bingley's openness. His £10,000 a year and Pemberley estate are established.

6.modern-en: Begins watching Elizabeth with interest, drawn to her 'fine eyes' and playful manner. She is oblivious.

8.modern-en: At Netherfield with Elizabeth nursing Jane. Defends Elizabeth's fine eyes when Miss Bingley mocks her.

10.modern-en: Engages in verbal sparring with Elizabeth. She accuses him of finding fault in everyone; he admits his temper is resentful.

11.modern-en: Admits Elizabeth could tempt him. Tries to guard himself against her charm.

12.modern-en: Relieved when Elizabeth leaves Netherfield, feeling she threatens his self-control.

16.modern-en: Wickham tells Elizabeth that Darcy denied him the living promised by Darcy's late father. (This is Wickham's lie.)

18.modern-en: Dances with Elizabeth at the Netherfield ball. Goes cold when she mentions Wickham.

26.modern-en: Mentioned as being in London with Bingley. Elizabeth suspects he is keeping Bingley from Jane.

30.modern-en: Arrives at Rosings with Colonel Fitzwilliam. Keeps watching Elizabeth.

31.modern-en: Seeks out Elizabeth at Rosings gatherings. His behavior puzzles her.

32.modern-en: Visits Elizabeth alone at the parsonage. Charlotte suspects his feelings.

33.modern-en: Colonel Fitzwilliam reveals Darcy recently saved a friend from an 'imprudent' match — meaning Jane and Bingley.

34.modern-en: Proposes to Elizabeth, unable to repress his feelings despite her inferior connections. She rejects him furiously.

35.modern-en: Delivers a letter explaining everything: Wickham's true character, the attempted elopement with Georgiana, and his honest belief that Jane did not love Bingley.

36.modern-en: His letter forces Elizabeth to reconsider everything she thought she knew.

43.modern-en: Arrives at Pemberley unexpectedly while Elizabeth is touring his estate. Instead of coldness, he is warm, attentive, and eager to introduce her to Georgiana.

44.modern-en: Introduces Elizabeth to Georgiana. Treats the Gardiners with genuine respect, shocking Elizabeth.

45.modern-en: Continues to seek Elizabeth's company at Pemberley.

46.modern-en: Elizabeth tells him about Lydia's elopement with Wickham. He leaves abruptly, distressed.

50.modern-en: Mentioned in the settlement discussion. Elizabeth suspects more money was involved than her uncle could manage alone.

51.modern-en: Lydia accidentally reveals Darcy attended her wedding.

52.modern-en: Mrs. Gardiner reveals the truth: Darcy tracked down Wickham, paid all his debts, bought his commission, and arranged the marriage — refusing to let Mr. Gardiner take any credit.

53.modern-en: Returns to Netherfield with Bingley. Visits the Bennets but is quiet and restrained.

54.modern-en: Still reserved during visits. Elizabeth cannot read his feelings. Mrs. Bennet snubs him at dinner.

56.modern-en: Lady Catherine tells him about Elizabeth's refusal to promise she would reject him. He takes it as encouragement.

58.modern-en: Walks with Elizabeth and proposes again. She accepts. He tells her Lady Catherine's visit gave him hope.

59.modern-en: The engagement is revealed. Mr. Bennet is shocked and wants to be sure Elizabeth truly loves him.

60.modern-en: Writes to Lady Catherine. Elizabeth reassures her father that she genuinely loves Darcy.

61.modern-en: Marries Elizabeth. They settle at Pemberley in lasting happiness. He and Bingley remain close.

3.modern-en: The beauty of the ball. Bingley dances with her twice and singles her out. She is quietly pleased.

4.modern-en: Tells Elizabeth she admires Bingley greatly. Characteristically sees only the good in his sisters.

5.modern-en: Charlotte and Elizabeth discuss whether Jane should show her feelings more openly to Bingley.

7.modern-en: Rides to Netherfield in the rain on Mrs. Bennet's scheme and catches a bad cold, forcing her to stay.

8.modern-en: Ill at Netherfield, tended by Elizabeth. Bingley is attentive and concerned.

9.modern-en: Still recovering at Netherfield when Mrs. Bennet visits.

12.modern-en: Returns home with Elizabeth after recovering.

17.modern-en: Hears Wickham's story from Elizabeth and tries to see both sides, hoping both men are good.

18.modern-en: Dances with Bingley at the Netherfield ball and is visibly happy.

21.modern-en: Receives Caroline Bingley's letter saying the party has left for London, hinting Bingley may marry Georgiana Darcy. Jane is hurt but tries not to show it.

24.modern-en: Writes from London that Miss Bingley was cold and distant when she called. Begins to accept Bingley may not return.

26.modern-en: Still in London, quietly heartbroken. Miss Bingley has barely acknowledged her.

33.modern-en: Mentioned: Colonel Fitzwilliam reveals Darcy separated Bingley from a woman he deemed unsuitable — Jane.

35.modern-en: Darcy's letter explains he believed Jane did not love Bingley, based on her composure.

40.modern-en: Elizabeth reveals Darcy's proposal but not the part about Bingley. Jane is astonished.

46.modern-en: Her letters reveal Lydia's elopement with Wickham.

49.modern-en: Relieved that Lydia will be married, but worried about the family's reputation.

53.modern-en: Bingley returns. Jane tries to be calm but her feelings are obvious.

55.modern-en: Bingley proposes and she accepts. She is radiantly happy.

58.modern-en: Mentioned as Elizabeth and Darcy become engaged the same week.

59.modern-en: Elizabeth tells Jane about her engagement to Darcy. Jane is overjoyed.

61.modern-en: Marries Bingley. They eventually move near Pemberley to be close to Elizabeth and Darcy.

1.modern-en: A single man with a large fortune has taken Netherfield Park. Mrs. Bennet is determined her husband must visit him.

2.modern-en: Mr. Bennet visits Bingley, though he pretends he won't.

3.modern-en: Attends the assembly ball. Dances every dance, is charming and open. Dances with Jane twice.

4.modern-en: Described as easy-going and amiable — the opposite of Darcy. Clearly smitten with Jane.

7.modern-en: Invites the Bennets to dinner. Jane rides over and falls ill, staying at Netherfield.

8.modern-en: Attentive to the ill Jane at Netherfield.

10.modern-en: Cheerful and social at Netherfield while Elizabeth stays.

18.modern-en: Dances with Jane at the Netherfield ball. Clearly in love.

21.modern-en: Has left Netherfield for London with his entire party. Caroline hints he will not return.

33.modern-en: Mentioned: Darcy separated him from Jane, believing she was indifferent.

35.modern-en: Darcy's letter confirms he convinced Bingley that Jane did not love him.

44.modern-en: At Pemberley with Darcy. Asks warmly after Jane.

53.modern-en: Returns to Netherfield. Visits the Bennets and is clearly still in love with Jane.

54.modern-en: Visits again and his feelings for Jane are obvious to everyone.

55.modern-en: Proposes to Jane and is accepted.

61.modern-en: Marries Jane. They eventually settle near Pemberley.

1.modern-en: Announces Netherfield is let at last and insists Mr. Bennet must visit the new tenant for the sake of their daughters.

2.modern-en: Furious that Mr. Bennet won't describe Bingley, then ecstatic when she learns he already visited.

3.modern-en: Delighted by the ball. Jane was admired! But she detests Mr. Darcy for slighting Lizzy.

7.modern-en: Schemes to send Jane to Netherfield on horseback in the rain so she'll have to stay the night.

9.modern-en: Visits Netherfield and thoroughly embarrasses the family with her vulgarity.

13.modern-en: Dreads Mr. Collins's visit, fearing he will throw them out of Longbourn.

18.modern-en: Loudly boasts at the ball about Jane marrying Bingley, within Darcy's hearing.

20.modern-en: Furious at Elizabeth for refusing Collins. Threatens never to see her again.

23.modern-en: Laments that Collins will throw them into the hedgerows when Mr. Bennet dies.

41.modern-en: Thrilled to send Lydia to Brighton with the regiment.

47.modern-en: Hysterical over Lydia's elopement. Takes to her bed.

49.modern-en: Overjoyed when she learns Lydia will be married after all.

53.modern-en: Mrs. Bennet is ecstatic that Bingley has returned. Insufferably rude to Darcy.

54.modern-en: Snubs Darcy openly at dinner, still holding a grudge from the first ball.

55.modern-en: Beside herself with joy at Jane's engagement to Bingley.

59.modern-en: Initially speechless at Elizabeth's engagement to Darcy, then ecstatic about his £10,000 a year.

61.modern-en: Both daughters married to rich men. Her life's mission accomplished.

epithet.en: The father, dry wit and detachment

1.modern-en: Teases his wife about visiting Bingley, pretending he won't go. Favors Lizzy for her sharpness.

2.modern-en: Reveals he has already visited Bingley, having planned to all along.

14.modern-en: Amused by Mr. Collins's pomposity. Enjoys him as entertainment.

15.modern-en: Finds Collins endlessly ridiculous. 'He is as absurd as I had hoped.'

20.modern-en: Supports Elizabeth's refusal of Collins. Tells her she would lose one parent either way.

41.modern-en: Dismisses Elizabeth's warning about Lydia going to Brighton. Refuses to intervene.

47.modern-en: Goes to London to search for Lydia. Realizes his negligence as a father contributed to this.

48.modern-en: In London searching for Lydia and Wickham.

50.modern-en: Returns home, chastened and ashamed. Admits he should have listened to Elizabeth.

57.modern-en: Finds the idea of Darcy proposing to Elizabeth hilarious — he cannot imagine it.

59.modern-en: Shocked by the engagement. Asks Elizabeth seriously if she truly loves Darcy.

60.modern-en: Satisfied after Elizabeth explains how her feelings changed. Gives his blessing.

61.modern-en: Misses Elizabeth but visits Pemberley often, especially the library.

2.modern-en: Boldly declares she isn't afraid of Mr. Bingley despite being the youngest — she's the tallest.

6.modern-en: Mentioned as flirtatious and boy-crazy with her sister Kitty.

39.modern-en: Returns from the militia camp full of gossip about officers.

41.modern-en: Invited to follow the regiment to Brighton. Elizabeth warns their father, but he lets Lydia go.

46.modern-en: Has eloped with Wickham. Jane's letters reveal they have run off together from Brighton.

47.modern-en: The family is in crisis. It emerges she left a note saying she expected to be married.

48.modern-en: Still missing with Wickham. The family fears the worst.

49.modern-en: Found. Wickham has been persuaded to marry her through financial arrangements.

51.modern-en: Returns home married, shameless and boastful. Accidentally reveals Darcy was at the wedding.

61.modern-en: She and Wickham are always short of money. Elizabeth and Jane help them out financially.

epithet.en: Charming officer with a dark past
epithet.da: Charmerende officer med en mørk fortid

15.modern-en: Arrives in Meryton as an officer. Handsome and charming. He and Darcy see each other and both go pale.

16.modern-en: Tells Elizabeth that Darcy denied him a living promised by Darcy's late father. His story is a calculated lie.

17.modern-en: Elizabeth tells Jane about Wickham's story. Jane hopes both men can be right somehow.

18.modern-en: Notably absent from the Netherfield ball, supposedly because of Darcy.

26.modern-en: Has abandoned Elizabeth and is now pursuing Miss King for her £10,000 inheritance.

35.modern-en: Darcy's letter reveals the truth: Wickham wasted his inheritance, demanded more money, then tried to elope with Georgiana Darcy for her £30,000.

36.modern-en: Elizabeth realizes everything Wickham told her was a lie.

41.modern-en: Stationed in Brighton with the regiment.

46.modern-en: Has eloped with Lydia, apparently with no intention of marrying her.

47.modern-en: Believed to have massive debts in Meryton. The family fears he never meant to marry Lydia.

48.modern-en: Mr. Gardiner is searching for him in London.

49.modern-en: Found and persuaded to marry Lydia through a financial settlement.

51.modern-en: Arrives at Longbourn as Lydia's husband, brazen and unashamed.

52.modern-en: Mrs. Gardiner reveals Darcy paid all of Wickham's debts and bought his commission.

61.modern-en: Always short of money, always asking Elizabeth and Jane for help. Unformed.

13.modern-en: Writes an absurd letter announcing his visit, full of self-importance. He is the heir to Longbourn through the entail.

14.modern-en: Arrives and proves every bit as ridiculous as his letter. Reads Fordyce's Sermons aloud until Lydia interrupts.

15.modern-en: Learns Jane may be spoken for and shifts his matrimonial attention to Elizabeth.

18.modern-en: Dances badly at the Netherfield ball. Introduces himself to Darcy uninvited, embarrassing Elizabeth.

19.modern-en: Proposes to Elizabeth in a long, pompous speech listing his reasons. She refuses firmly; he cannot believe it.

20.modern-en: Mrs. Bennet tries to force Elizabeth to accept. Mr. Bennet backs Elizabeth. Collins is offended.

22.modern-en: Proposes to Charlotte Lucas, who accepts him. He recovers from Elizabeth's rejection with remarkable speed.

28.modern-en: Elizabeth visits the Collinses at Hunsford. He shows off his house and his patroness Lady Catherine endlessly.

29.modern-en: Presents Elizabeth to Lady Catherine at Rosings, groveling with every breath.

57.modern-en: Writes to Mr. Bennet warning against Elizabeth accepting Darcy, citing Lady Catherine's displeasure.

61.modern-en: Continues as rector of Hunsford, toadying to Lady Catherine.

5.modern-en: Discusses Jane and Bingley with Elizabeth. Argues Jane should show her feelings more openly.

6.modern-en: Talks to Elizabeth about the need for practicality in marriage. Her views foreshadow her own choice.

22.modern-en: Accepts Mr. Collins's proposal three days after Elizabeth's refusal. She is 27, plain, and without fortune. A pragmatic choice.

28.modern-en: Elizabeth visits Hunsford and finds Charlotte managing Collins and her household with quiet competence.

32.modern-en: Suspects Darcy is in love with Elizabeth after his visits to the parsonage.

61.modern-en: Continues her sensible, if loveless, marriage to Collins.

14.modern-en: Collins speaks of his patroness with reverent awe before Elizabeth meets her.

29.modern-en: Elizabeth dines at Rosings. Lady Catherine is imperious, condescending, and loves to give her opinion on everything.

30.modern-en: Continues to dominate every conversation at Rosings.

31.modern-en: Elizabeth stands up to Lady Catherine's questioning with composure.

56.modern-en: Travels to Longbourn to confront Elizabeth, demanding she promise never to accept Darcy. Elizabeth refuses absolutely.

57.modern-en: Lady Catherine writes angrily to Collins. Her report of Elizabeth's refusal inadvertently encourages Darcy.

58.modern-en: Darcy reveals Lady Catherine's visit gave him hope — Elizabeth's refusal to promise meant she might accept him.

61.modern-en: Eventually reconciles with Darcy and Elizabeth and even visits Pemberley.

21.modern-en: Caroline hints Bingley may marry Georgiana Darcy, using her to try to separate Bingley from Jane.

35.modern-en: Darcy's letter reveals Wickham attempted to elope with Georgiana when she was fifteen, for her £30,000 fortune.

44.modern-en: Darcy introduces her to Elizabeth at Pemberley. She is shy and sweet, not proud as Wickham claimed.

45.modern-en: Visits with Elizabeth at Pemberley. Goes pale when Miss Bingley mentions Wickham.

61.modern-en: Becomes like a sister to Elizabeth at Pemberley.

3.modern-en: Attends the assembly ball. Stylish and sophisticated.

4.modern-en: Elizabeth sees through the Bingley sisters' false warmth toward Jane.

6.modern-en: Tries to get Darcy's attention. He is watching Elizabeth instead.

8.modern-en: Mocks Elizabeth's muddy petticoats and her family's low connections.

10.modern-en: Jealous of Darcy's attention to Elizabeth. Tries to draw him away.

11.modern-en: Walks about the room with Elizabeth, trying to catch Darcy's eye.

21.modern-en: Writes to Jane that the whole party has left for London, hinting at Georgiana as a match for Bingley.

24.modern-en: Cold and dismissive when Jane calls on her in London.

45.modern-en: At Pemberley, tries to unsettle Elizabeth by mentioning Wickham.

61.modern-en: Eventually accepts Elizabeth as Darcy's wife and maintains the relationship for her brother's sake.

2.modern-en: Asked for her opinion on Bingley but struggles to say something suitably wise.

5.modern-en: Offers ponderous reflections on pride versus vanity.

18.modern-en: Performs at the Netherfield ball with more zeal than talent, embarrassing her family.

47.modern-en: Offers moral platitudes about Lydia's disgrace that help no one.

61.modern-en: With her sisters married and gone, she becomes less competitive and more agreeable.

2.modern-en: Coughs and is scolded by her mother. Her father jokes about her timing.

39.modern-en: Returns from meeting the regiment, echoing Lydia's obsession with officers.

41.modern-en: Devastated that Lydia gets to go to Brighton and she does not.

47.modern-en: Distraught over Lydia's elopement and the family crisis.

61.modern-en: Spends time at Pemberley and Bingley's home, improving away from Lydia's influence.
